                "Difficulty": "Moderate-Easy",
                "ItemType": "MCQ",
                "ItemStyle": "single-select",
                "Stem": "Umbra wants to maintain a constant 12-month planning horizon. Which response is most appropriate?",
                "Choices": {
                        "A": "Use rolling budgets only for capital projects",
                        "B": "Add a new future month or quarter as the current period is completed",
                        "C": "Replace the budget only after a recession",
                        "D": "Freeze the budget for the entire strategic plan period"
                },
                "CorrectChoice": "B",
                "ExplanationCorrect": "A rolling budget continuously updates by adding a new period as the latest period ends.",
                "StudyLinks": [
                        {
                                "label": "IMA CMA Learning Outcome Statements, Part 1 Section B",

                ],
                "ExplanationWrongA": "Rolling budgets are not restricted to capital projects; they are equally applicable to operating budgets, sales forecasts, cash budgets, production plans, and any other area that benefits from a continuous forward-looking horizon. The defining characteristic is maintaining a constant planning window — typically 12 months — by adding a new period each time a period concludes. This continuous-update mechanism is agnostic to budget category and is widely used across all functional areas, not just capital expenditures.",
                "ExplanationWrongB": "",
                "ExplanationWrongC": "A rolling budget is updated on a regular periodic schedule — typically monthly or quarterly — not in response to economic events or recessions. Waiting for a recession to trigger a budget replacement means the planning horizon shrinks between updates, defeating the purpose of maintaining a constant forward-looking view. The rolling budget mechanism drops the elapsed period and appends a new future period on a fixed calendar basis regardless of economic conditions.",
                "ExplanationWrongD": "Freezing a budget for the full strategic plan period directly contradicts the continuous-update principle at the heart of rolling budgets. Under a rolling budget, the completed period is dropped and a new future period is added on a regular schedule, ensuring the planning horizon remains at a constant length. A frozen budget becomes increasingly disconnected from actual conditions as time passes, whereas a rolling budget adapts continuously.",
